{{Short description|Analytic function with prescribed zeros}}
[[File:Blaschke-product.png|thumb|Blaschke product, <math>B(z)</math>, associated to 50 randomly chosen points in the unit disk. <math>B(z)</math> is represented as a [[Matplotlib]] plot, using a version of the [[Domain coloring|domain coloring]] method.]]

In [[complex analysis]], a '''Blaschke product''' is a bounded [[analytic function]] in the open unit disc constructed to have zeros at a finite or infinite sequence of prescribed [[complex number]]s <math>a_0,a_1,\ldots</math> inside the [[unit disc]], with the property that the magnitude of the function is constant along the boundary of the disc.

Blaschke products were introduced by [[Wilhelm Blaschke]] in 1915.<ref name="Blaschke1915">{{cite journal
 |last=Blaschke
 |first=Wilhelm
 |author-link=Wilhelm Blaschke
 |title=Eine Erweiterung des Satzes von Vitali über Folgen analytischer Funktionen
 |language=de
 |journal=Berichte Math.-Phys. Kl. Sächs. Gesell. der Wiss. Leipzig
 |volume=67
 |year=1915
 |pages=194–200
 |url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015036849837;view=1up;seq=226}}</ref> They are related to [[Hardy space]]s.<ref name="Tamrazov">{{eom
 |title=Blaschke product
 |first=P. M.
 |last=Tamrazov
 |mode=cs1}}</ref>

==Definition==

A sequence of points <math>(a_n)</math> inside the unit disk is said to satisfy the '''Blaschke condition''' when

:<math>\sum_n(1-|a_n|)<\infty.</math>

Given a sequence obeying the Blaschke condition, the Blaschke product is defined as

:<math>B(z)=\prod_n B(a_n,z)</math>

with factors

:<math>B(a,z)=\frac{|a|}{a}\frac{a-z}{1-\overline{a}z}</math>

provided <math>a\neq0</math>. Here <math>\overline{a}</math> is the [[complex conjugate]] of <math>a</math>. When <math>a=0</math>, take <math>B(0,z)=z</math>.

The Blaschke product <math>B(z)</math> defines a function analytic in the open unit disc and vanishing exactly at the points <math>a_n</math>, with [[Multiplicity (mathematics)|multiplicity]] counted. Furthermore, it belongs to the Hardy class <math>H^\infty</math>.<ref name="Conway1996">{{cite book
 |last=Conway
 |first=John B.
 |author-link=John B. Conway
 |title=Functions of a Complex Variable II
 |series=[[Graduate Texts in Mathematics]]
 |volume=159
 |publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]]
 |year=1996
 |page=274
 |isbn=0-387-94460-5
 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JN0hz3qO1eMC&pg=PA273}}</ref>

The sequence <math>(a_n)</math> satisfying the convergence criterion above is sometimes called a ''Blaschke sequence''.

==Szegő theorem==

A theorem of [[Gábor Szegő]] states that if <math>f\in H^1</math>, the [[Hardy space]] with integrable norm, and if <math>f</math> is not identically zero, then the zeroes of <math>f</math>, which are at most countable, satisfy the Blaschke condition.

==Finite Blaschke products==

Finite Blaschke products can be characterized as analytic functions on the unit disc in the following way.<ref name="Colwell1985">{{cite book
 |last=Colwell
 |first=Peter
 |title=Blaschke Products
 |publisher=University of Michigan Press
 |location=Ann Arbor, Michigan
 |year=1985
 |isbn=0-472-10065-3
 |mr=779463}}</ref> Assume that <math>f</math> is analytic on the open unit disc and can be extended to a continuous function on the closed unit disc

:<math>\overline{\Delta}=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|\leq1\}</math>

that maps the unit circle to itself. Then <math>f</math> is equal to a finite Blaschke product

:<math>B(z)=\zeta\prod_{i=1}^n\left(\frac{z-a_i}{1-\overline{a_i}z}\right)^{m_i},</math>

where <math>\zeta</math> lies on the unit circle, <math>|a_i|<1</math>, and <math>m_i</math> is the multiplicity of the zero <math>a_i</math>. In particular, if <math>f</math> satisfies the condition above and has no zeros inside the unit circle, then <math>f</math> is constant. This fact is also a consequence of the [[maximum principle]] for [[harmonic function]]s, applied to the harmonic function <math>\log|f(z)|</math>.

==Asymptotics of powers==

For <math>0<\rho<1</math>, consider the Blaschke factor

:<math>b_\rho(z)=\frac{z-\rho}{1-\rho z}</math>

and write

:<math>b_\rho(z)^n=\sum_{k\geq0}\widehat{b_\rho^n}(k)z^k.</math>

Set

:<math>\alpha_0=\frac{1-\rho}{1+\rho}.</math>

When <math>n</math> is large and <math>k</math> is proportional to <math>n</math>, the asymptotic behavior of these coefficients changes at the two indices <math>\alpha_0 n</math> and <math>\alpha_0^{-1}n</math>. If <math>k/n</math> remains in a compact subinterval of <math>(\alpha_0,\alpha_0^{-1})</math>, the coefficients have oscillatory stationary-phase asymptotics of order <math>n^{-1/2}</math>. Outside this interval they decay exponentially. An Airy-type asymptotic near the transition point <math>\alpha_0^{-1}n</math>, approached from inside the interval <math>(\alpha_0 n,\alpha_0^{-1}n)</math>, is established in this setting.<ref name="SzehrZarouf2020">{{cite journal
 |last1=Szehr
 |first1=Oleg
 |last2=Zarouf
 |first2=Rachid
 |title=ℓ<sup>''p''</sup>-norms of Fourier coefficients of powers of a Blaschke factor
 |journal=Journal d'Analyse Mathématique
 |volume=140
 |issue=1
 |year=2020
 |pages=1–30
 |doi=10.1007/s11854-020-0090-y}}</ref> More generally, near either endpoint, on the scale <math>|k-\alpha_0^{\pm1}n|=O(n^{1/3})</math>, the transition is described by the [[Airy function]], and the largest coefficients are of order <math>n^{-1/3}</math>.<ref name="BorichevFouchetZarouf2024CA">{{cite journal
 |last1=Borichev
 |first1=Alexander
 |last2=Fouchet
 |first2=Karine
 |last3=Zarouf
 |first3=Rachid
 |title=On the Fourier Coefficients of Powers of a Blaschke Factor and Strongly Annular Functions
 |journal=Constructive Approximation
 |volume=60
 |issue=1
 |year=2024
 |pages=33–86
 |doi=10.1007/s00365-023-09650-4}}</ref>

For <math>1\leq p\leq\infty</math>, the corresponding asymptotic orders of the <math>\ell^p</math>-norms of the Taylor coefficients are

:<math>
\left\|\widehat{b_\rho^n}\right\|_{\ell^p}
\asymp
\begin{cases}
n^{\,1/p-1/2}, & 1\leq p<4,\\[4pt]
\left(\dfrac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/4}, & p=4,\\[8pt]
n^{\,1/(3p)-1/3}, & 4<p\leq\infty,
\end{cases}
</math>

where <math>1/\infty=0</math> and the implicit constants depend on <math>p</math> and <math>\rho</math>.<ref name="SzehrZarouf2020"/>

For general finite Blaschke products, the asymptotic size of the largest coefficient of <math>B^n</math> is similarly determined by the maximal degeneracy of the stationary points of the boundary phase of <math>B</math>.<ref name="BorichevFouchetZarouf2024IMRN">{{cite journal
 |last1=Borichev
 |first1=Alexander
 |last2=Fouchet
 |first2=Karine
 |last3=Zarouf
 |first3=Rachid
 |title=On the Fourier Coefficients of Powers of a Finite Blaschke Product
 |journal=International Mathematics Research Notices
 |volume=2024
 |issue=20
 |year=2024
 |pages=13255–13280
 |doi=10.1093/imrn/rnae199}}</ref>
